security_audit.summary: The static findings are documentation examples for MCP URLs, environment variable placeholders, shell snippets, and troubleshooting checks. I found no executable installer scripts, embedded secrets, unauthorized network calls, or prompt injection text in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Example credentials and URLs can trigger automated scanner matches.
remediation.suggestion: Keep placeholders clearly labeled and avoid realistic secret values in future examples.

remediation.issue: Shell helper snippets may be copied into user environments.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to review helper scripts and avoid loading untrusted .env files.

content.user_title: Configure MCP Servers for Claude Code Plugins
content.value_statement: Adding external tools to Claude Code plugins can be confusing and security-sensitive. This skill explains MCP server types, authentication, configuration files, and testing steps.
actual_capabilities: Explains .mcp.json and inline mcpServers configuration options.
Compares stdio, SSE, HTTP, and WebSocket MCP server types.
Shows authentication patterns for OAuth, bearer tokens, headers, and environment variables.
Describes MCP tool naming and allowed-tools configuration.
Provides testing and troubleshooting steps using /mcp and debug logs.
Includes example configurations for stdio, SSE, and HTTP servers.
limitations: Does not provide a working MCP server implementation.
Does not verify third-party endpoint security or OAuth scopes.
Requires developers to validate commands, paths, and credentials before publishing.
Examples use placeholders and must be adapted for each service.

use_cases.title: Add a Hosted Service
use_cases.description: Configure an SSE or HTTP MCP server for a cloud service with OAuth or token authentication.

use_cases.title: Standardize Plugin Integrations
use_cases.description: Create repeatable patterns for server type selection, environment variables, and README setup instructions.

use_cases.title: Review MCP Permissions
use_cases.description: Check planned MCP tools, authentication settings, secure URLs, and wildcard permissions before publication.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Basic Server
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one hosted MCP service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add a simple SSE MCP server to my Claude Code plugin. Ask for the service URL, authentication method, and required tools before drafting the configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Server Type
prompt_templates.scenario: Select the best MCP transport for a service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare stdio, SSE, HTTP, and WebSocket MCP options for my plugin use case: [describe service]. Recommend the safest configuration and required README notes.

prompt_templates.title: Design Authentication
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan credential handling for an MCP integration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an MCP authentication setup for [service]. Include required environment variables, OAuth or token flow, secure storage notes, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Multi-Server Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before publishing a plugin.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this planned MCP plugin integration: [describe servers, tools, permissions]. Identify risky defaults, wildcard tool access, credential exposure, and test cases.

output_examples.input: User asks to add a hosted project management MCP server.
output: Recommended server type: SSE, because the service is hosted and supports OAuth.
Required setup: document the service URL, OAuth flow, scopes, and expected tools.
Security note: pre-allow only the task tools needed by plugin commands.

output_examples.input: User asks how to pass an API token to an HTTP MCP server.
output: Use an environment variable for the token and document the variable name.
Avoid placing token values in plugin files or examples.
Test missing, expired, and insufficient-scope token cases.

output_examples.input: User asks why MCP tools do not appear after configuration.
output: Check that the server is connected in the MCP status view.
Confirm the tool name prefix matches the plugin and server names.
Restart Claude Code after configuration changes and review debug logs.

best_practices: Use HTTPS or WSS and document every required environment variable.
Pre-allow only the specific MCP tools needed by commands or agents.
Test connection, authentication, tool calls, and error cases before publishing.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding access tokens, passwords, or workspace IDs in plugin files.
Using wildcard MCP tool permissions for routine commands.
Shipping stdio commands that accept unsanitized user-controlled arguments.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps developers configure MCP servers for Claude Code plugins and connect external tools safely.

faq.question: Which MCP server type should I choose?
faq.answer: Use stdio for local tools, SSE for hosted OAuth services, HTTP for token APIs, and WebSocket for real-time streams.

faq.question: Does this skill install MCP servers automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Developers must configure, review, and test their own MCP servers.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Store secrets in user environment variables or OAuth flows. Do not commit token values to plugin files.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is written for Claude Code plugins and is searchable for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code users.

faq.question: What should I check before publishing?
faq.answer: Verify secure URLs, scoped credentials, exact tool permissions, documented setup, and graceful error handling.
